turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, Mr. Iyer. I have just checked you. Blood pressure is one thirty-eight over eighty-six, pulse is seventy-eight, and oxygen is ninety-four percent on room air. Temperature is thirty-six point six.

[SEG0002] person_1 (NURSE): Spirometry is also done. FEV1 is one point six litres, fifty-eight percent predicted. FVC is two point four litres, and the ratio is sixty-six percent. The printout is on the file.
[SEG0003] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ramesh, come in, sit comfortably. Lakshmi, you also please sit. How have you been keeping?
[SEG0004] person_3 (PATIENT): I am fine only, doctor. A small cough in the morning, that is all. No need for all this drama.
[SEG0005] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, he will minimise everything. Every morning he coughs, and on the flat road to the shop he stops to catch his breath.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ramesh, tell me in your own words. What is this cough like for you?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Morning time itself it starts, little phlegm, then it is quiet. It is there since many years. Dust and weather, nothing more.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): And this breathlessness your wife is describing, when do you feel it?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Only if I walk fast. Um, maybe two weeks it is a little more, after that small cold. I am managing.
[SEG0010] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two weeks, he says. It is at least one month, doctor. And three weeks back he was properly down with fever.
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Arre, two days of fever and it went. A small cold. Why stretch it?
[SEG0012] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He was bringing green phlegm. The nearby doctor called it a chest infection and gave an antibiotic. He did finish the tablets.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you remember the antibiotic, the strength, and how many days?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): Amoxicillin, five hundred milligram, three times a day, for five days, for that chest infection. Finished. Done.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever now, any pain in the chest, any blood in the phlegm?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): No fever now. No chest pain. No blood. I am telling you, it is nothing.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about the inhalers at home, how are you actually using them?

[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): Blue one is Asthalin, two puffs when I feel tight. Brown one is budesonide, two hundred microgram morning and night, they said. Morning I take if I remember. Night I forget, what to do.
[SEG0019] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That brown inhaler stays in the drawer, doctor. Most days he does not touch it. I have watched.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): So it was meant twice a day, and it is going in only now and then. Thank you, that helps me.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the smoking, how does a usual day look?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): About ten a day... maybe twenty. I am not a heavy smoker. Only cigarettes, from a long time. I can stop when I decide.
[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Some days the packet is finished, so twenty is more honest than ten.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long have you been smoking, roughly?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): From when I was eighteen. I am sixty-two now. Still not a problem, see, I am sitting here talking.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Are you still working, and any alcohol?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): Retired from the bank, three years. A small peg of whisky, well, actually only on the weekend, not daily.
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, just to say, the drive from Adyar was terrible. We sat near the flyover for forty minutes, not moving.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): That road has become a headache. Were you able to hear the cricket at least, stuck like that?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): India were batting. The opener was set nicely, then a silly run out. My grandson was on the phone, shouting the whole time.
[SEG0031] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The boy had his school annual day yesterday, a dance with costumes, and still he talks only about the match. We saw the highlights twice after dinner.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Annual day is a full production in these schools. Did he like being on the stage?
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): Very much. Now he wants to be a fast bowler, not a dancer. Children change every week.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let him enjoy both, no harm. Ramesh, may I listen to your chest now?
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): There is a soft wheeze on both sides. I do not hear crackles. The chest is moving, though a little less than I would like.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): See, wheeze can be from anything. I feel alright sitting.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any loss of weight lately? And bowels, urine, all quiet?
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): Weight is the same. Motions are normal. Urine also no problem.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any operation in the past? Any allergy to a medicine or a food?
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): No operation ever. No allergy. I can take whatever you give.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anyone in the family with a breathing problem like this?
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): My father had breathing trouble in his last years. He smoked also. It is just the family way, not some special disease.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has a doctor put a name to this before?
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): They said COPD, two years back. I am not that bad as the word sounds. I manage.

[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. My working impression is a flare of your COPD, the recent chest infection mostly settled, and the spirometry shows obstruction. We will not call it anything final beyond that.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please take the budesonide morning and night, every day, not only when you remember. Keep the Asthalin for when the chest feels tight.
[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): I will try, doctor. These pumps are a nuisance, but I will try.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): For the cigarettes, I would like to start nicotine gum, two milligram by mouth, one piece when the urge comes, maximum eight pieces in a day.
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): Gum I don't need. I can leave it myself. Ten or twenty is not such a big matter, I told you.
[SEG0050] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He has been saying he will stop since last year. Please write the gum. I will keep it where he can see it.

[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): I will write the gum today. Our quitting counsellor can also see you. If you are willing, I will ask reception to book that, and the offer stays open even if you say no now.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the breathlessness and cough have not settled by the next visit, we might do a CT scan of the chest. Nothing like that today.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): I want to see you in two weeks either way, and Lakshmi can come along. If you get more short of breath, or fever or blood returns, do not wait for that date.
[SEG0054] person_3 (PATIENT): Two weeks, ok ok, I will come. All this scan business is extra, I am fine.
[SEG0055] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will bring him, doctor. Don't worry.
[SEG0056] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Bring both inhalers next time so we can check how you use them. Safe journey back, and wish that young bowler from me.
[SEG0057] person_3 (PATIENT): I will bring the two pumps. Come, Lakshmi, traffic will be bad again if we sit here.

omissions.text: Oxygen saturation was 94% on room air.
Morning cough was described as small/little with a little phlegm, quiet after the morning, and triggered/worsened by dust and weather.
Patient reported breathlessness only if he walks fast and said he was managing; family member specifically said he stops to catch his breath on the flat road to the shop.
There is a disagreement about the severity of smoking: patient first said about 10 a day and then maybe 20, while family member said some days he finishes a packet and 20 is more honest.
Current budesonide adherence is poor: patient said he takes the morning dose only if he remembers and forgets the night dose; family member said most days he does not touch it.
Doctor advised specifically to take budesonide every day, not only when remembered.
Negative finding missing: no current problem with urine and motions/bowels normal were recorded as ROS, but the explicit answer that bowels and urine were 'all quiet' was part of direct questioning.
No operations ever in the past.
